newsitem.title: MALAWI: World Bank lends Malawi $56 million.
newsitem.headline: World Bank lends Malawi $56 million.

text.p: The World Bank has loaned Malawi 850 million Malawi kwacha ($56.7 million) for over 200 development projects to help eradicate poverty, a government minister said on Thursday.

Finance and Economic Planning Minister Aleke Banda said at the commemoration of the International Year for the Eradication of Poverty that Malawi had adequate funds for its development projects but needed hard work from its citizens.
"There is no excuse that there is no money," he said.
Although the World Bank approved the funding in May this year, it was publicly revealed on Thursday for the first time.

Banda said the economy began improving after the government effectively reversed destabilising factors of the currency flotation implemented by the former government before it was ejected in the first multi-party elections in 1994.
"Malawians can expect a further drop in the bank interest rates before the end of this calendar year," he said.
The Reserve Bank of Malawi in September cut its base lending rate to 35 percent from 45 per cent, the second reduction since it was first cut from 50 percent in June.
Banda said Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was expected to grow by nearly 11 percent this year.
Smallholder farmers have produced two million tonnes of maize this year compared to 1.5 million last year, he said.
